ex.train_sbatch:
#!/bin/bash
# The running example on Slurm: 2 nodes x 2 ranks. One torchrun per node (srun starts them), c10d rendezvous
# on the first node of the allocation. Submit as a lab user: su alice -c "sbatch /shared/jobs/train.sbatch"
# Extra arguments go to train.py, e.g. sbatch train.sbatch --steps 400 --step-sleep-ms 50. RUN names the output dirs.
#SBATCH --job-name=mi-train
#SBATCH --nodes=2
#SBATCH --ntasks-per-node=1
#SBATCH --cpus-per-task=2
#SBATCH --gres=gpu:2
#SBATCH --time=00:10:00
#SBATCH --output=/shared/out/%x-%j.out
#SBATCH --requeue
set -euo pipefail
export MASTER_ADDR=$(scontrol show hostnames "$SLURM_JOB_NODELIST" | head -n1)
export MASTER_PORT=29500
RUN=${RUN:-slurm-$SLURM_JOB_ID}
echo "job $SLURM_JOB_ID nodes $SLURM_JOB_NODELIST master $MASTER_ADDR:$MASTER_PORT restart ${SLURM_RESTART_COUNT:-0}"
srun --kill-on-bad-exit=1 torchrun --nnodes="$SLURM_NNODES" --nproc-per-node=2 \
  --rdzv-backend=c10d --rdzv-endpoint="$MASTER_ADDR:$MASTER_PORT" --rdzv-id="$SLURM_JOB_ID" \
  /opt/mi/train.py --ckpt-dir "/shared/ckpt/$RUN" --log-dir "/shared/logs/$RUN" "$@"
ex.sig_script:
#!/bin/bash
# Checkpoint before the time limit: Slurm sends SIGUSR1 to the batch shell 25 s before the limit;
# the trap saves (here: prints) and requeues the job, which resumes on its next start.
#SBATCH -J sl-sig
#SBATCH --time=1
#SBATCH --signal=B:USR1@25
#SBATCH --requeue
#SBATCH -n1 --gpus-per-task=1 --cpus-per-task=1
#SBATCH -o /shared/out/sl/%x-%j.out
#SBATCH --open-mode=append
echo "$(date -u +%T) start on $(hostname), SLURM_RESTART_COUNT=${SLURM_RESTART_COUNT:-0}"
if [ "${SLURM_RESTART_COUNT:-0}" -ge 1 ]; then echo "$(date -u +%T) resuming from the saved checkpoint"; sleep 5; echo "$(date -u +%T) finished"; exit 0; fi
trap 'echo "$(date -u +%T) got SIGUSR1: saving checkpoint, then requeue"; scontrol requeue $SLURM_JOB_ID; echo "requeue exit $?"; exit 0' USR1
sleep 300 & wait

#!/bin/bash
# A heterogeneous job: component 0 is one CPU-only task (a launcher or data server), component 1 is two GPU nodes.
#SBATCH -J sl-het
#SBATCH --time=2
#SBATCH -o /shared/out/sl/%x-%j.out
#SBATCH -N1 -n1 --cpus-per-task=1
#SBATCH hetjob
#SBATCH -N2 --ntasks-per-node=1 --gpus-per-task=2 --cpus-per-task=2
echo "batch on $(hostname): het group 0 nodes=$SLURM_JOB_NODELIST_HET_GROUP_0, group 1 nodes=$SLURM_JOB_NODELIST_HET_GROUP_1"
srun --het-group=0 bash -c 'echo "group0 $(hostname) gpus=${SLURM_GPUS_ON_NODE:-0}"'
srun --het-group=1 -l bash -c 'echo "group1 $(hostname) gpus=$SLURM_GPUS_ON_NODE"'
srun --het-group=0,1 -l hostname
